summary: Build-script caching drops Cargo-recognized rerun environment declarations surrounded by whitespace and silently restores stale generated output.
scenario: A normal build.rs prints a stable file declaration and "  cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=APP_MODE  ", then writes APP_MODE into OUT_DIR/value. With baseline Kache as RUSTC_WRAPPER, Cargo builds first with APP_MODE=first and then second. Both builds succeed but the executable includes first twice; plain Cargo produces first then second.

evidence.point: Cargo-facing declaration parser applies line.trim() before rerun_directive.
Run-cache prediction parser calls rerun_directive(line) without trimming, omitting the padded APP_MODE declaration.
Run action key folds only the environment names retained in prediction.env.
Recording a successful script run constructs its prediction using parse_declarations.
A compiled build_script_build installs the production launcher, proving reachability through ordinary Cargo.
Second successful Cargo build returns first and records a build_script_run local_hit with the first key.
Plain Cargo on the same fixture semantics produces first, second.

trace: Cargo builds script → wrapper installs launcher → main dispatches KACHE_BUILD_SCRIPT_PATH → run_shim/run_cached → record_with_tools/parse_declarations omits APP_MODE → action_key excludes changed APP_MODE → local_hit replays old OUT_DIR/value → newly built executable prints first.

authority.quote: Kache reuses Cargo's own rule for when a build script must rerun. Every variable the script declared with cargo:rerun-if-env-changed is covered; Cargo trims instruction lines.

severity: Silent wrong compiled contents rather than a diagnostic: generated configuration, bindings or selected features can remain stale even though Cargo recognizes the declared change. Default build-script cache reaches the defect; scope requires padded declaration lines. Demonstrated with non-hermetic cache and one macOS Rust toolchain; no general cross-platform scope claim.

summary: Dropping the executable from test-runner lease arguments does not lose target identity in the current global lock design.
checked: Read target-use locking and test-runner/delegate callers. shared_for arguments select quiet output only; shared obtains cache_dir/target-use.lock globally. No runtime race claim inferred from omitted executable argv.

evidence.point: Global target-use.lock protects the cache; argument scan only changes notice sink.
Production runner holds target-use lease while executing child and deciding cache reuse.
